source_reconstruction: E24 saved models/optimizers/anchors but not the global torch RNG used by its reservoirs. Reconstruct each source by rerunning the exact 8192-batch E24 prefix from seed+400000. Require every recorded prequential error and all behavior-relevant model, optimizer, anchor, context, counter and control state to match the saved checkpoint exactly. Retain the reconstructed global RNG and charge prefix replay separately. The 16384-batch world must preserve every original prefix x, y and clean target. No source is excluded because its previous result failed. Preserve and reuse verified reconstruction artifacts if execution resumes.
causal_comparison: All three arms start from identical reconstructed model/memory/RNG states and continue the same 8192 new batches. Underlying E6 observe behavior is unchanged. The active arm calls its predictor with count=False; separate query counters charge actual prediction work in every arm. Candidate selection changes only operational predictions. After each real output arrives, the underlying E6 learner updates first, then the router may train on observed data. Router sampling uses a private RNG and initialization preserves the core global RNG. Every final core learning state and global RNG must agree exactly across the three arms. This is a full-feedback supervised continuation, not a closed-loop counterfactual-action experiment.
stable_slots: Persistent experts use slots 0..module_cap-1; a live temporary expert always uses slot module_cap. Query/training masks exclude absent slots. Cache invalidation uses persistent count, temporary presence, merge count and event count, not Python object addresses. A merged or discarded temporary expert cannot remain selectable through a stale cache. Missing slots never receive an oracle identity.
nearest_cached: Build nearest-anchor expert labels from minimum per-example squared error of current experts on pooled actual anchors/scratch records. Normalize using that cache's observed mean/std (std clamped at 0.1). Refresh every 128 observed batches and when the library signature changes. Prediction uses the label of the closest normalized stored input, then evaluates only that selected expert. No query output enters a past prediction. Cache target evaluations, normalized inputs, labels and distance pairs count.
online_top1: Use an 8-to-16-tanh-to-(module_cap+1) router with validity-masked logits. If multiple experts exist initially, bootstrap for 256 Adam 0.01 batches of 64 sampled from actual retained observations. Afterwards take one Adam update per real batch when multiple experts are available. The training batch combines the current 32 observed inputs/targets and 32 private-RNG samples from current pooled memory. Targets are current experts' lowest observed-error slots, computed after the core update. The input normalization is fixed when this router is first initialized, avoiding unannounced coordinate changes beneath learned weights. If the run begins with one expert, defer router allocation; first later multiexpert use initializes it with one ordinary update, not an uncharged bootstrap. Learned routing state persists through all future changes. Single-expert queries bypass routing; any previously allocated router state remains counted.
evaluation: Record causal prequential clean error and all operational routing/fit work. Every 512 batches evaluate fresh fixed common and rare probes drawn using seed+2600000, never supplied to any learner. Common probes mix all four previously observed means; rare probes use the original rare law. Also record the explicitly privileged best retained expert for each probe region, including temporary experts. These diagnostic targets do not train or select a router. Report every source/arm, all errors and failures, final persistent state, and any expert-library changes. The same historical world continues; these are not eight newly acquired worlds.
preflight: On disjoint dummy streams exercise changing expert availability, verify predictions precede current outputs, valid masked choices, changed learned router parameters, private/global RNG separation and identical core states across all three selectors. Verify exact saved/restored core and router prediction/state continuation. Scored source reconstruction additionally requires exact full-prefix errors and state equality. Do not weaken equality thresholds after seeing a mismatch.
costs: Separate inherited E24 work and charged prefix reconstruction from new learner work. Record core forward/update deltas, query expert examples, router query examples, nearest distance pairs, target-construction expert examples, router training examples and backward batches, cache refreshes, initial fitting time and actual loop time. Probe forwards/times are audit work and included separately in study costs. Add all persistent router/cache/normalization/optimizer/private-RNG tensors to inherited core storage. A source's reconstruction is shared across arms and charged once, not three times or zero times. Full process/peak autograd RAM, complete FLOPs and energy are unmeasured. Supervised stream length is not autonomous planning horizon.
falsification: A frozen retrieval gain may disappear with stale labels, new experts, merges, missing evidence or drifting competencies. Compare learned online selection with the cheaper periodically refreshed nearest-anchor rule, including fitting costs and rare-query regressions. Exactly equal core trajectories isolate access from core-learning changes; they do not establish an improved world model or preservation of information absent from all experts. This integrates online learned access with persistent model learning and bounded memory, but does not demonstrate recursive self-application, novelty or general reasoning. After this integration, prioritize the missing ordered-reasoning component instead of indefinitely tuning supervised routing.
